requirements.statement: When a re-proof (`/verify-build --criteria <ids> --no-fix --chained`) finishes its one iteration with any named criterion not `met`, it re-runs only those criteria exactly once more, with no code edit and no Debug stage, and the second result is the one taken. Must pass: yes.
requirements.source: TRD Objectives table, row O1 (source: owner instruction 2026-11-11, roadmap item 3)

requirements.statement: A criterion met on the retry is recorded as `met` with `retried: true` in `.trd-state/<feature>/reverify/verification-state.json` (the file the custody gate reads), so the ship proceeds and the flake stays visible. A criterion still not met after the retry ends the ship as today (custody refuses, the run stops). Must pass: yes.

The subset keeps its paths under `.trd-state/<feature>/reverify/` and ends on the existing `[STATUS: /verify-build] RETURN → <outcome>, <met> of <total> met` line, counted over the whole named subset after the retry. Must pass: no (not marked).
The retry set and the merge of the two runs are computed by a library function with unit tests, not by the model. Must pass: no (not marked).
requirements.source: TRD Objectives table, row O4 (acceptance: a unit test of whatever library computes the retry set)

open_questions: OQ-1: Does a not_verifiable or unbuilt criterion get the retry, or only not_met? Assumed: all non-met statuses are retried (custody refuses all alike; a preview still coming up reads not_verifiable). Owner-only: no (blank in TRD).
could_not_verify: A live re-proof with one deliberately flaky criterion in a fixture slot, showing met-on-retry: deferred by the roadmap until this item is built; the unit and prose tests cannot show a model actually follows the new steps.

The retry helps a flaky check, not an environment that is slow to come up: it starts immediately with no wait, so a preview still building at the first run will usually fail the setup check again on the retry (verify-functional.js:1367-1371 marks every open criterion not_verifiable on a setup failure) [read]. The retry still runs for it; it is just unlikely to change the result.
